item.title: Facilities FAQ template and free Excel worksheet for tenant helpdesks
item.description:
Facilities FAQ template for tenant helpdesks

Use the Excel template to turn current building policy into short, approved answers for common tenant questions. Each entry records where the answer comes from, when it should be checked and who handles exceptions.

Download the free Excel FAQ template Use the shift handover checklist

How to write an approved FAQ answer

  1. Choose one recurring question

    Group questions that ask for the same outcome. Start with a routine request such as visitor parking, delivery hours or where to submit a maintenance issue. State which building the answer applies to.

  2. Write from the current building policy

    Use the approved source to write a short answer that gives the tenant a clear next step. Record the source title and revision, the approving role and the next review date. Have that role approve the answer for use.

  3. Define when staff should take over

    Name who handles missing information, requests for approval and situations outside policy. Specify the context the receiving team needs, such as the building and the question. For emergencies, use the building’s existing emergency channels.

  4. Test different ways tenants ask

    Check the standard question and a variation such as “Where can my guest park?” Both should give the same approved answer. Test an unclear question and one outside policy, such as a weekend parking request, to verify that the helpdesk asks for clarification or routes it to staff.

Fictional example for visitor parking

Building A, its policy and the dates below are fictional.

Tenant question
How do visitors arrange parking?
Example answer
At Building A, the tenant hosting the visit registers the guest with reception through the tenant portal before arrival. Reception confirms availability and any charges under the current visitor parking policy.
Policy source
Use this answer for standard visits at Building A. Source is the Visitor Parking Policy, revision 2, dated 20 November 2026. The property manager approves the answer. Next review is 20 December 2026.
When to hand off
Send same-day exceptions, weekend requests and questions about parking fees or validation to reception. Reception checks the current policy and confirms the arrangements.

Review before publishing or updating

  • Have someone who did not write the entry check that each instruction follows the approved source.
  • Confirm the answer applies to the named building, visit type and operating hours.
  • Check that staff receiving an exception can see the question, the location and the next action.
  • Review affected entries when the building policy changes and replace outdated answers or withdraw them.
  • 101 California tenant manual, including visitor and garage procedures

item.title: After-hours HVAC request form for commercial buildings | BigPlanner Partners
item.description:
After-hours HVAC request form

Use this checklist and blank form to request planned heating, ventilation or air conditioning outside normal hours in a commercial building. The tenant provides the area and local times, and the building team confirms what it can schedule.

Download the editable text form View the blank form

When to use this form

Use it to extend service for planned evening, weekend or holiday occupancy. For a room that is already scheduled for service and has weak or failed heating or cooling, use the building’s maintenance request process. For an emergency, follow the building’s established procedures.

Check the tenant handbook or ask building management for standard hours, advance notice, minimum run times, any fees and how to make or cancel a request. These rules can vary by site and day.

What to include in the request

  • Who is requesting service. Give the tenant organization, the authorized contact and a work contact for changes.
  • The area to serve. Identify the building, floor, suite or room. Include the HVAC zone if it is known.
  • The requested window. Give the date and local start and end times. For a request crossing midnight, include the end date. For a recurring request, list the dates or the recurrence and its end date.
  • The service and any cost approval. State what service is needed and include the billing reference or approval the building requires, if applicable.

How to confirm and schedule service

  1. The property or facilities team verifies the authorized contact, served area, requested times and site rules. It asks for missing information or proposes a different window when needed.
  2. Authorized staff approve or decline the request. The reply gives the request reference, approved area and local time window, and any applicable charges or conditions. Pending requests retain an owner and a follow-up time.
  3. Facilities staff record the approved window in the building’s existing scheduling system. Changes or cancellations go through the same site process. The next shift can use the request reference to check the latest status.

Fictional request example

A tenant plans a Saturday workshop in a meeting room and requests cooling for that area.

Request reference
HVAC-EX-01
Area and times
Building A, fifth-floor meeting room. Saturday, 5 December 2026, 09:00 to 13:00 local time.
Tenant request
One-time cooling request from the tenant’s authorized office contact.
Staff confirmation
The duty property manager approves the room and time window. The facilities team records it in the building schedule and confirms the reference and window with the tenant.

Blank after-hours HVAC request form

Fill in the requested area and local times. Send the completed form through the building’s approved channel and use the confirmed window.

Request reference or date submitted

Building, floor, suite or room, and HVAC zone if known

End date and local time

item.title: Facilities shift handover checklist and free Excel log | BigPlanner Partners
item.description:
Facilities shift handover checklist

Pass open tenant requests to the next shift with the exact location, current owner and next check. The Excel workbook includes a blank log and a worked example for a commercial building.

Download the free Excel log

Before the outgoing shift leaves

  1. Use one ticket ID for the request. Record when it came in, in site-local time, and identify the building, floor and room.
  2. Summarise what the tenant reported and record any checks or actions already completed.
  3. Identify the person or team responsible. Add the current status, the next action and a due time or check-in time.
  4. Review open items with the incoming shift and confirm who will follow up.

For emergencies, follow the building’s established contacts and procedures.

Example handover entry

This example uses a fictional building and request. Times are local to the site.

Ticket and time
DEMO-012 · 5 October 2026, 20:35
Location
Building A, fifth floor, shared meeting room
Issue
A tenant reported weak cooling.
Owner and status
Morning facilities technician · In progress
Next check
6 October, 07:30 · Inspect the filter and check airflow.

See the same request move between shifts

The 27-second walkthrough shows how AI collects the details, a supervisor assigns the request and the next shift reads the same record. The walkthrough has a Korean interface and English captions.
